Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. Our procurement team is comfortable with most of the Order Form, but Legal flagged the publicity clause and wants a clearer statement on logo use and reference rights before we finalize. Specifically: do you require pre-approval for every press mention that includes Redwood? Can Helios include Redwood in customer lists and a one-line case study on our site without prior sign-off?

If you have a short redline or summary that captures Redwood's standard position on: (1) press releases, (2) logo usage in partner/customer materials, and (3) permission to list as a reference, that would help speed sign-off on our end.

Attached our internal checklist for the review.

Thanks,

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the detailed note. Short answers up front: we usually require a 48-hour courtesy review for press releases that quote either party and explicit brand asset approvals for logo use. We don't prohibit listing Redwood as a customer or a one-line case reference, but we ask that case-study drafts or testimonial quotes be shared for review before publication.

I'll pull together a short redline to the publicity clause and loop in Legal to confirm language around logos and testimonial approvals. Ben, can you attach the standard publicity redline you shared with Sales last quarter? Marissa, would you mind taking a quick look once I have the draft?

Sofia

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Helios' note. I drafted a short redline to the Order Form publicity section and summarized the asks in the attached. Key points:
- Redwood requests 48-hour review for press releases that reference Redwood or include quotes.
- Logo use permitted for co-marketing with prior brand asset approval; Helios may display Redwood logo on customer lists and sales materials (small logo) without pre-approval if usage matches the brand guidelines; for larger marketing assets or press ads we require pre-approval.
- Permission to list as a reference is granted; for case studies and testimonial quotes we request draft review and final sign-off.

I've attached: Helios_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (track changes) and publicity_redline_summary.pdf (one-page). Please advise on any legal/contractual concerns or stronger wording you'd recommend. If Legal is comfortable, I'll send back to Rachel with the updated doc.

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I reviewed the redline doc and made two small legal edits (tracked in the attached PDF):
1) Clarified that the 48-hour courtesy review applies to press releases that include direct quotes or deal-specific financials; generic announcements ("we are now using Redwood Inference") do not require sign-off, only notification.
2) Added language to the logo section that permits listing on customer pages and in partner directories without prior approval provided the logo is used at a size and resolution consistent with our brand guidelines; anything that implies endorsement (e.g., case study headline claiming outcome percentages) needs prior written approval.

If that's acceptable to Helios, we can incorporate these edits and sign the Order Form. Rachel — copying Helios Legal per your original thread so they can confirm locally.

Marissa Cole
